title: The Cohutta Cat: An Adventure Bikepacking Race
content:
Every fall, a small crew of bikepackers gathers around Ellijay, Georgia for one of the Southeast’s most brutal grassroots races: the Cohutta Cat. Known by some as the “little brother” of the TNGA, this figure-8 route packs 260 miles and over 30,000 feet of climbing into some of the gnarliest terrain in the Cohutta Wilderness — and some riders choose to tackle all of that on little to no sleep.

This year’s edition brought new race director Matt Schweiker, a stacked crew chasing the FKT, torrential overnight rain, at least one bloody crash, and some fun finish line drama. We followed the riders from the start line in Mulberry Gap through the resupply in Blue Ridge and all the way to the finish to capture what it actually takes to survive a self-supported ultra-endurance bikepacking race.
